source.what: FlowSpace locations index (flowspace.framer.website/locations): the directory page of the FlowSpace coworking template. A large 'Our Locations' title over a one-line positioning statement, then a two-control filter bar (a name search field and a city dropdown) above a three-column grid of six photo location cards with scrim overlays and View pills, closing on a rounded black CTA panel with a feature list and an avatar counter, then the black footer. Monochrome UI, one family, three-quarter-step card entrance stagger.
source.method: Node + puppeteer-core driving local Chromium (ms-playwright build). Loaded at 1440x900, 834x1112, 390x844; entrance animations sampled at 90ms intervals from first paint to read durations, delays, easings and per-property keyframes before the reveals finished, then all animations advanced to their end state so every still is settled. Full-page and fold stills per width. Computed-style probes on the H1, subtitle, filter labels and wrappers, search input, city select, grid cards, card names and addresses, the CTA panel, its Contact pill and trailing icon orb, the feature rows, the avatar stack and the footer. Behaviour probes: typing 'tui' into the search field, reading the six city options, selecting Paris, typing an impossible query, and measuring grid geometry at all three widths.
gaps: The no-results state was not resolved. Typing an impossible query into the search field removed the visible cards but the probe's card detector still matched five wrapper nodes and no message string containing 'no location' or 'no result' was found in the page text. Whether the template prints an empty-state line, hides the grid entirely, or shows a zero-count is unknown.

Card filtering is confirmed to work (search 'tui' narrows the rendered cards to Tuileries; selecting Paris narrows to Tuileries) but the transition between filtered states was not characterised: whether cards animate out, fade, or re-run the entrance stagger is unverified.

Hover and focus states on the filter controls, the View pills and the Contact pill were not probed. The wrapper's border is drawn on its ::after pseudo-element rather than the element itself, which the hover machinery used here does not reach.

The city select is a native select. Its option list, its open state and any custom dropdown panel could not be captured because a native select popup is outside the page's DOM; only the closed control and its six options are recorded.
The avatar row's images are demo portraits; their source set and any hover behaviour were not captured. The stack is measured as four 32px circles overlapping by 8px.

The CTA panel's Contact pill carries a second, hidden text container in the DOM (a duplicated 'Contact us' label at a different y offset), which the probe caught as two text rows. The visible rendered pill shows one label plus the icon orb; the duplicate is treated as an unused hover-slide artefact and its animation state was not confirmed.

The 10s opacity fade registered on the subtitle container (opacity 0.001 to 0.001, effectively invisible) is unresolved; it appeared in the timeline on load on the sibling Tuileries page too, and completes before measurement here.
DM Sans and Inter load with the document but render no visible text; only Plus Jakarta Sans was observed rendering.
Several wrapper nodes compute the default link blue rgb(0,0,238) without rendering blue, as on the sibling pages.

Template content is placeholder: six demo locations across three demo cities, demo portraits, hello@yourcoworking.com and +33 6 12 34 56 78. A real deployment would carry real addresses and a real city set.
Validation is partial: discrimination was measured against the two sibling FlowSpace page rubrics but a full sensitivity/invariance pass and a blind re-score are not yet recorded on this page.
Production use requires human sign-off on this frozen file.
source.notes: Third of three FlowSpace page rubrics, after flowspace_home_v1 and flowspace_property_single_v1. This page is the directory: it is the only one of the three with a filter bar, the only one that renders the location card as a grid tile rather than a single wide panel, and the only one where the card set is staggered in on load. Type scale, pill system, card radius, scrim gradient and footer are inherited from the template and match the sibling rubrics exactly. Discrimination: measured 48% of canon scales differing by 2.0 or more against flowspace_home_v1 (above the one-third bar), but only 8% against flowspace_property_single_v1. That second figure is expected rather than a defect: both are detail pages of one template and they share the container, the tile size, the scrim ramp, the CTA panel, the type scale, the pill system and the footer. The two pages separate almost entirely on motion (energy 5.0 vs 1.0, temperament 5.0 vs 1.5) because this page staggers its grid in and the property page is static. Use this rubric for the directory behaviour (filter bar, six-tile grid, staggered entrance) and the sibling for the single-listing behaviour (sticky rail, photo cluster, tabs).

parts.name: Location card entrance stagger
parts.description: The six location cards do not appear: they arrive in reading order, each fading up from opacity 0.001 and translateY(16px) to rest, 100ms behind the one before it. The cascade runs delays 400/500/600/700/800/900ms at 800ms per card on cubic-bezier(0.12,0.23,0.17,0.98), so the last card lands about 1700ms after paint. The H1 above it is split per glyph and blurs in separately, and the subtitle is a separate element that fades and rises on its own 200ms delay.
parts.entry_test: Remove the stagger and the page is a static grid of six tiles with no sense of a set being populated. The wave sweeping the grid in reading order is how this page announces that it holds a list rather than a single listing, and it is the only motion on the page with any duration to it.

anchor.value: the six grid tiles under [data-framer-name='LocationsList'], and the h1 glyph spans above them

parts.recipe: Wrap each grid card so it can carry its own animation. Per card: animate opacity from 0.001 and transform from translateY(16px) to opacity 1 and transform none, 800ms on cubic-bezier(0.12,0.23,0.17,0.98), delay 400ms plus 100ms per card index. Split the H1 into per-glyph spans and give each the same ease over 800ms with a filter blur from 4px to 0; give the subtitle 800ms on a 200ms delay with the same 16px rise.

parts.name: Two-control filter bar
parts.description: The directory is narrowed by exactly two controls sitting side by side above the grid: a free-text name search and a city dropdown, each a 240x40 field under a 12px label, both drawn as hairline-bordered rounded rectangles. There is no chip row, no sort control, no result count and no reset button. The whole filtering apparatus is two fields and 16px of gutter, which is what keeps a six-item directory from looking like a database.
parts.entry_test: Replace the bar with a row of city chips and the page gains a control that has to be styled, wrapped and scrolled on mobile. The two-field bar is the page's entire interaction model, and it is what makes 'Our Locations' read as a small curated set rather than a search product.
parts.recipe: Lay out a two-item row with a 16px gap: each item is a 12px label above a 240x40 field. Give each field a 1px rgba(0,0,0,0.1) border and an 8px radius drawn on the wrapper's ::after pseudo-element, with 12px of inner padding. The first field holds a small magnifier glyph and a 14px input placeholdered 'Search…'; the second wraps a native select showing 'All' with a chevron at its right edge. Do not add a submit button: both controls filter live.

parts.name: Three-column directory grid
parts.description: The directory is a strict three-up grid of equal 363x400 photo tiles on a 16px gutter, dropping to two columns at 834 and one at 390. The columns land on x160 / x539 / x917 at desktop: a 379px pitch made of a 363px card and a 16px gap. Rows advance by 416px, the card's 400px height plus the same 16px gap. Every tile is the same size regardless of how many locations the city holds, so the grid stays a grid.
parts.entry_test: Let the tiles size to their content and the page loses the even lattice that makes six locations comparable at a glance. The fixed 363x400 tile on a 16px gutter is what lets the eye scan across rows, and it is the same card geometry the single-property page uses for its other-locations pair.
parts.recipe: Three equal columns inside the 1120px container with a 16px gap and 16px row gap. Each tile is fixed at 363x400 (a 0.91 ratio, taller than wide) with a 16px radius. At 834w step down to two columns of 385px; at 390w collapse to a single 358px column. Do not let the tile height follow the image or the address length.

parts.name: White pill with a solid icon orb
parts.description: The CTA's Contact pill is a white capsule containing the label at the left and a solid black circle at the right, the circle holding a mail glyph. The geometry is asymmetric: 168x48 with 24px radius and padding of 0 4px 0 24px, so the left inset is 24px against a 4px right inset that keeps the orb nearly touching the pill edge. The orb is 40 by 40 with a 50% radius, leaving 4px of white between it and the pill's own edge.
parts.entry_test: Replace the orb with a plain arrow or drop it and the pill becomes an ordinary white button. The solid circle capping the capsule is the template's signature control, it repeats on the home page's CTAs, and the 4px right inset that pins it to the edge is what makes the pill read as a container for the orb rather than a label with an icon.

limitations: The no-results state is unresolved: typing an impossible query removed the visible cards, but the card detector still matched five wrapper nodes and no empty-state string appeared in the page text. Whether the template prints a message, hides the grid, or silently shows nothing is unknown and should not be asserted when generating from this rubric.

Card filtering is confirmed functional (search 'tui' narrows to Tuileries; selecting Paris narrows to Tuileries) but the transition between filtered states was not characterised — whether cards animate out, fade, or replay the entrance stagger is unverified.

Hover and focus states on the filter controls, the View pills and the Contact pill are unverified. The filter border lives on the wrapper's ::after pseudo-element, which the hover probe used here cannot reach.

The city select is a native select, so its open state, option styling and any custom dropdown panel are outside the page DOM and were not captured; only the closed control and its four options are recorded.

The Contact pill contains a second, hidden 'Contact us' text container in the DOM at a different y offset. The rendered pill shows one label plus the orb; the duplicate is treated as an unused hover-slide artefact whose animated state was not confirmed.
A 10s opacity fade (0.001 to 0.001, effectively invisible) runs on the subtitle container on every load, as on the sibling pages. Its purpose is unresolved and it completes before measurement.
DM Sans and Inter load with the document but render no visible text; only Plus Jakarta Sans was observed rendering.
Wrapper nodes computing the default link blue rgb(0,0,238) appear here as on the sibling pages and are treated as not part of the design.
Template content is placeholder: six demo locations across three demo cities, demo avatar portraits, hello@yourcoworking.com and +33 6 12 34 56 78.
Validation is partial: discrimination was measured against the two sibling FlowSpace page rubrics, but a sensitivity pass, an invariance pass and a blind re-score are not yet recorded on this page.
The 834w and 390w grid measurements come from the capture's own stills plus a re-viewport probe; intermediate breakpoints between 390 and 834 were not measured.
Production use requires human sign-off on this frozen file.
